name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+24 district with a nationally prominent incumbent
Jeffries has raised $17.5M; challenger shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price the race near 98% Democratic
No public polling, but no signs of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's 24-point Democratic lean, Jeffries' stature as House Democratic Leader, and an overwhelming financial asymmetry against an unknown, unfunded challenger leave essentially no path for an upset; markets agree at roughly 98% Democratic.
model.watch: Only a dramatic shift in challenger visibility or an unexpected national environment could narrow the margin, and even that would be unlikely to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-08 in Brooklyn is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, and Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic Leader, is seeking another term. He has raised more than $17 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Lewis Mizrahi shows no reported fundraising or outside spending. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 98 percent, and no serious general-election polling exists for the race.

With no measurable challenger activity, the contest functions as a low-profile race on paper. The district's 24-point Democratic lean, combined with the usual incumbency and money advantages, points to a comfortable Jeffries win. The main uncertainty is turnout in a race drawing little attention, which could shave a few points off the margin but is very unlikely to change the outcome.
